market_summary: Markets are whipsawing on a hot October CPI print that pushed Treasury yields higher, with the S&P 500 and Nasdaq selling off Tuesday before a tech-led futures rebound Wednesday. Nvidia is the epicenter of volatility — down over 25% in a month on a Baird downgrade (PT cut to $200 from $500) and fresh reputational/legal headline risk tied to its CEO, with earnings due Nov 17. In Singapore, bank Q3 results were mixed: OCBC beat and hit a record nine-month profit while DBS and UOB missed, dragging the STI down 2.2% for the week; SIA posted a strong Q2 but H1 profit nearly halved on jet fuel costs.

picks.thesis: Nvidia has become a battleground stock: a rare sell-side downgrade (Baird to Neutral, PT slashed from $500 to $200) alongside Morgan Stanley pulling it as a Top Pick, plus a serious reputational/espionage-adjacent headline about the CEO, have combined with a stretched prior run-up to produce a sharp breakdown. Price is down 5.5% today alone on 3x normal volume, -25% in a month, and trading well below its 50/200-day averages — classic momentum-breakdown signature. Earnings on Nov 17 add binary event risk into an already de-risking market structure.
picks.news: Baird cut NVDA to Neutral with PT to $200 from $500 citing 2027 demand visibility and supply constraints (2026-11-11); Morgan Stanley removed it as a Top Pick on a stop-loss trigger after a 25% decline (2026-11-11); reports of a CEO personal/reputational scandal with national-security overtones hit the stock the same day (2026-11-11).
picks.risks: Nvidia remains the most-loved name on the Street (58 buys vs 3 holds/1 sell) and any reassuring Nov 17 earnings beat or guidance could trigger a violent short-covering rally; the CEO-scandal story could also prove overstated or quickly resolved.

picks.thesis: OCBC was the only one of the three Singapore banks to beat Q3 estimates, posting a record nine-month net profit of S$6.24bn, up 10% y/y, while DBS and UOB both missed. This earnings-quality divergence, combined with OCBC still trading ~10.7% below its 52-week high and above its 200-day average, supports relative outperformance versus peer banks over the coming weeks as the market digests the Q3 season.
picks.news: OCBC Q3 2026 net profit of S$2.04bn beat the S$2.01bn consensus and record 9M profit of S$6.24bn, up 10% y/y (2026-11-06).
picks.risks: Banks are trading on compressed trading-income and rate-sensitive margins; a further leg down in regional rates or a broad STI selloff (STI -2.2% last week) could drag OCBC down with the sector regardless of its earnings beat.

picks.thesis: DBS missed Q3 consensus with net profit down 5% y/y to S$2.81bn, driven by a 65% collapse in markets trading income — a clear earnings quality problem. The stock is already underperforming, down 5.9% versus its 50-day average and -7.2% over the past month, suggesting the market is still repricing lower after the miss.
picks.news: DBS Q3 2026 net profit fell 5% to S$2.81bn, missing the ~S$2.90bn consensus, with markets trading income down 65% (2026-11-03).
picks.risks: DBS retains a strong consensus buy skew (11 buy/5 hold/1 sell) with 10%+ implied upside to target; any stabilization in trading income or a dividend/buyback announcement could quickly reverse the post-earnings weakness.

picks.thesis: UOB's Q3 profit missed consensus by a wide margin (S$1.25bn vs S$1.38bn expected) and fell 15% q/q, triggering an immediate ~5% share price drop. Momentum remains weak — the stock is down 7.2% over the month, 9.9% over three months, and trading below both its 50- and 200-day averages, reflecting ongoing disappointment with the bank's trajectory despite a flattering year-on-year comparison.
picks.news: UOB Q3 2026 profit of S$1.25bn missed the S$1.38bn consensus and fell 15% q/q; shares fell ~5% on the results (2026-11-04).
picks.risks: Analyst base is split (5 buy/9 hold/2 sell) with ~10% implied upside to target, and any dividend surprise or guidance reset at the next update could support the stock; low conviction given mixed sell-side views.

picks.thesis: Keppel is signaling it will return 10-15% of asset-monetisation proceeds (already ~S$940m realized, another ~S$600m targeted by year end) as special dividends, a shareholder-friendly catalyst layered on top of a heavily discounted valuation — analysts see ~28% upside to consensus target with 12 of 15 rating it a buy. The stock's weak recent momentum (down ~5% over a month, 24.8% below 52-week high) may already price in much of the bad news, leaving room for a re-rating once a specific special dividend is declared.
picks.news: Keppel plans to pay out 10-15% of asset monetisation proceeds as FY2026 special dividends, though none has been declared yet; ~S$940m already realized with ~S$600m more targeted by end-2026 (2026-11-11).
picks.risks: No special dividend has actually been declared yet, so this is a show-me story; continued macro weakness in Singapore property/industrials or delays in monetisation could keep the stock range-bound or falling further given its current downtrend (below both 50- and 200-day averages).
